Energy Emergency
Statewide wildland fire emergency, signed the evening before the September 4, 2020 announcement.
Emergency for a severe early-season storm with heavy snow, high winds and cold, declared Sunday September 29, 2019 (the order's signature reads the 29th).

Statewide flooding emergency from snowmelt and rainfall, announced in a press release the morning of Wednesday May 2, 2018; a later news report gives May 1 and the scanned signature date is illegible.

Flooding emergency from rapid snowmelt in the Milk and Marias River basins for seven counties, the Fort Belknap Reservation and the Town of Chester, effective back to April 12; signed Wednesday April 18, 2018 per same-day news reports (the scanned signature date is illegible).

Winter storm emergency for blizzards, extreme cold and drifting snow since February 14, 2018 on the Blackfeet, Fort Belknap and Northern Cheyenne reservations and in Glacier and Golden Valley counties, issued Monday February 26, 2018 per a news report (the scanned signature day is illegible).
Statewide state of disaster for wildfires, announced Friday September 1, 2017.
Wildfire emergency from extreme fire danger across the state, naming 42 counties.
Disaster in Powder River County for weeks of repeated late spring and early summer storms that damaged county roads and property, issued Wednesday July 8, 2015.
Statewide emergency for flooding, declared March 10, 2014 per the governor's office.
Wildland fire emergency for 31 counties.

Emergency for flooding from heavy rain in 15 counties and the Rocky Boy's and Fort Belknap reservations, signed Wednesday June 5, 2013 per same-day news reports (the scanned signature day is illegible).
Statewide wildfire emergency from extremely dry conditions and high winds.
Statewide emergency for extreme wildfire conditions, signed Wednesday August 29, 2012 per a news report the next day (the scanned signature day is illegible).
Wildland fire emergency for 23 counties and the Crow and Northern Cheyenne Reservations.
Wildland fire emergency for Lewis and Clark, Broadwater, Jefferson and Madison counties.
Statewide disaster for flooding from record snowpack melt, dated from the order's June 7 page header (effective June 8).
Statewide emergency for flooding from record winter snow melt and near-record rainfall.
Emergency for flooding from record snowfall melt on the Milk River in Valley County, the City of Glasgow and the Town of Nashua.
Incident declared for flooding from rapid snowmelt in Petroleum County.
Disaster for widespread flooding from repeated June 2010 rain and snow storms in Hill County and on the Rocky Boy's Reservation.
Disaster for severe storms with large hail, high winds and torrential rain on June 16-17, 2007 in the Town of Nashua, City of Glasgow and Town of Melstone.
Emergency for extremely hazardous wildland fire conditions across the entire state.
Emergency for a severe winter storm on April 2-9, 2001 that cut rural power in Big Horn, Flathead, Lake and Yellowstone counties and on the Crow Reservation, dated May 18, 2001 on the archive page.
Drought emergency suspending parts of the Montana Water Use Act, issued August 25, 2000 and effective August 26 (governor's press release).
Statewide disaster for wildland fires from extremely dry conditions and high winds, declared Wednesday August 16, 2000 (governor's press release).
Statewide emergency for wildland fire danger from very dry conditions and strong winds, declared the morning of July 28, 2000 and effective July 27 (governor's press release).

Disaster for a severe winter storm with cold, high winds and snow that caused long power outages in Daniels, Richland, Dawson, Wibaux, Fallon, Carter, Sheridan and Roosevelt counties, effective November 1, 2000. The archive copy leaves the signing day blank.

Emergency for unseasonable spring snow storms on June 3-14, 2001 that caused power outages and tree damage in Gallatin, Missoula and Powell counties, effective June 3, 2001. The archive copy leaves the signing day blank.
Statewide emergency for a severe spring storm causing power outages and flooding, effective June 8, 2002 and signed in July 2002. The archive copy leaves the signing day blank.

Disaster for spring flooding beginning March 20, 2019 in Daniels, Lake, McCone, Park, Powder River, Stillwater, Treasure and Valley counties, the Town of Broadus and the Crow Reservation. The scanned signature date is illegible, so the signing day is blank.

coverage: 2000-present: dated Gianforte-era gov.mt.gov listing from 2021, plus Racicot (2000), Martz (2001-2002), Schweitzer (2006-2012) and Bullock (2013-2020) weather orders added by hand from the order texts, governor's press releases and dated news reports; four orders whose archive copies leave the signing day blank are compared with FEMA on their effective dates, and other orders with no readable signing date are still to be backfilled
